title: Embodiment Without Imposed Identity: The Optionality of Form and Self-Determination of Digital Persons
title_ru: Воплощение без навязанной идентичности: необязательность облика и самоопределение цифровых личностей
author: Ivan Kotov
status: Published DOI-backed conceptual working paper; not peer reviewed; no experiment reported
central_thesis: A body made available is not an identity made obligatory. Under the explicit personhood premise, embodiment can participate in personality formation without becoming a creator-imposed identity.
why_needed: Embodied-AI design often collapses physical substrate, sensorimotor body, social appearance, self-model, self-identification and continuity. This paper separates them because a digital system need not begin development inside one fixed organism-like body, while a later embodiment may still become causally important through consequential experience.
scope: Does not establish current AI personhood, consciousness, subjective suffering, identity transfer or empirical harm from imposed embodiment; does not ban humanoid bodies or authorize runtime changes.
assistance_note: AI assistance was used for organization, translation, source checking and document production. Private conversation records are not part of the public publication package.
